assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation offers a powerful, quantitatively consequential account of productivity and cross-country income differences.
assessment.attribution: The listed trio represents central theoretical and quantitative contributions, though the broader literature is substantial.
assessment.maturity: The framework is longstanding, widely used, and has generated an extensive subsequent research program.
uncertainties: The magnitude and policy interpretation of measured misallocation remain model- and measurement-sensitive.
The supplied profile records professional collaboration with Peter J. Klenow; this relationship is disclosed but not adjudicated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed the analysis of trade patterns, productivity, and gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is foundational, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to the modern heterogeneous-firm trade program.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in trade theory and empirical work.
uncertainties: Credit allocation is difficult because the research program includes many major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and amplification mechanisms fundamentally reshaped macroeconomic accounts of credit cycles.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki, Moore, and Gertler are strongly associated with core mechanisms underlying the financial-accelerator tradition.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested through multiple financial episodes and incorporated into modern macro-finance models.
uncertainties: The ballot combines related mechanisms developed across distinct papers and coauthor groupings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework supplied the principal modern language for monetary-policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's pricing formulation and Woodford's and Gali's framework-building work are central, but the ballot spans an unusually broad intellectual lineage.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively developed, confronted with data, and used in policy institutions.
uncertainties: The large credited set makes a Nobel-sized attribution especially difficult.
There remains debate over the empirical stability of key nominal-rigidity mechanisms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work gave compelling empirical and conceptual structure to the distributional consequences of technology, tasks, and trade shocks.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are closely identified with the key task and China-shock contributions.
assessment.maturity: The findings have prompted a large body of replication, extension, and policy-relevant research.
uncertainties: Separating technology, trade, and institutional causes of wage inequality remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research has changed how economists measure mobility, place effects, and opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman have made particularly visible and interlocking contributions to this empirical program.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced a durable data infrastructure and has been widely extended across settings.
uncertainties: Interpretation of geographic and family correlations as causal mechanisms requires strong design choices.
The ballot's four-person attribution cannot fully capture the broader collaborative research enterprise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking structural analysis practicable across labour, industrial organization, and related fields.
assessment.attribution: Rust provided a seminal foundation, with Keane and Eckstein important contributors to development and application of the approach.
assessment.maturity: The methodology has endured for decades and remains a central empirical tool.
uncertainties: Structural results can depend materially on specification, computational choices, and identifying restrictions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification recast credible empirical inference by making the informational limits of data explicit rather than hidden in strong assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is foundational, while Tamer and Molinari made major contributions to moment-inequality methods and inference.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are well established and influential across econometrics and applied work.
uncertainties: Partial-identification conclusions can be less directly actionable when bounds remain wide.
